proposals.before: Yang Shihou came from Jinchou in Yingzhou.
proposals.after: Yang Shihou came from Jingou in Yingzhou.
proposals.reason: 斤溝 is Jingou, not Jinchou; the place-name romanization is wrong.

proposals.before: Yang Shihou, a man of Jinchou in Yingzhou.
proposals.after: Yang Shihou, a man of Jingou in Yingzhou.
proposals.reason: 斤溝 is Jingou, not Jinchou; the place-name romanization is wrong.

proposals.before: After Baixiang the Jin had harried the frontier; Shihou marched the main host to Zhenzhou, burned villages, raided Gaocheng and Shulu, and withdrew from deep in Zhao territory.
proposals.after: Earlier, after our setback at Baixiang the men of Zhen had repeatedly raided the border; Shihou led the main army straight to Zhenzhou below the walls, burned and swept hamlets, shifted the army to plunder Gaocheng and Shulu, and returned from Shenzhou.
proposals.reason: 深州 is the prefecture Shenzhou, not “deep”; 鎮人 are men of Zhen.

proposals.before: Earlier, after our setback at Baixiang the Jin had repeatedly raided the border; Shihou led the main army straight to Zhenzhou below the walls, burned and swept hamlets, shifted the army to plunder Gaocheng and Shulu, and returned from deep in Zhao.
proposals.after: Earlier, after our setback at Baixiang the men of Zhen had repeatedly raided the border; Shihou led the main army straight to Zhenzhou below the walls, burned and swept hamlets, shifted the army to plunder Gaocheng and Shulu, and returned from Shenzhou.
proposals.reason: 深州 is Shenzhou; both English fields mistranslate 深 as “deep”.

proposals.before: Yan failed to get in; Cunjie alone rushed the west gate with hidden men and scaling ladders, took the bridge, and the whole force poured in.
proposals.after: Wang Yan could not enter; Cunjie alone led the hidden troops bearing ladders in a mass assault on the west barbican, seized the moat bridge, and all armies advanced together.
proposals.reason: 王言 is Wang Yan; idiomatic “Yan” wrongly looks like the place Yan (鄆).

proposals.before: Born Li, he received the style Zanzhen from the Founder.
proposals.after: His original name was Li; the Founder changed it and gave him his courtesy name.
proposals.reason: 本名禮，太祖改而字之: the Founder changed his name and styled him; “Born Li” is unnatural.

proposals.before: In year 5 he became prefect of Bo, soon Xuanyi commander, then governor of Su.
proposals.after: In year 5 he became prefect of Bo, soon Xuanwu commander, then governor of Su.
proposals.reason: Chinese 宣武軍 is the Xuanwu Army; Xuanyi is a wrong romanization of 宣武.

proposals.before: Year 5, he was made prefect of Bo; soon he was advanced to overall commander of the Xuanyi army and changed to prefect of Su.
proposals.after: Year 5, he was made prefect of Bo; soon he was advanced to overall commander of the Xuanwu army and changed to prefect of Su.
proposals.reason: Chinese 宣武軍 is the Xuanwu Army; Xuanyi misreads 宣武.

proposals.before: The Jin were fresh from victory and fierce; Cunjie pushed on, marched by night with gags, and reached Ze as the wall guards were already firing beacons and shouting to the relief force; prefect Bao Ya stood in the city in confusion.
proposals.after: The Jin were fresh from victory and fierce; Cunjie pushed on, marched by night with gags, and reached Ze as the wall guards were already firing beacons and shouting to the relief force; the prefect held the yamen city and did not know what to do.
proposals.reason: Chinese 刺史保衙城 means the prefect defended/held the yamen citadel; 保衙 is not a personal name Bao Ya.

proposals.before: At that time the Jin had just won and their edge was very sharp; Cunjie led his followers forward, marched at night with gags in the men's mouths, and reached Ze; he happened on the wall guards already lighting fires and shouting to answer the outside army; the prefect Bao Ya held the city and did not know what to do.
proposals.after: At that time the Jin had just won and their edge was very sharp; Cunjie led his followers forward, marched at night with gags in the men's mouths, and reached Ze; he happened on the wall guards already lighting fires and shouting to answer the outside army; the prefect held the yamen city and did not know what to do.
proposals.reason: Chinese 保衙城 is 'held the yamen city,' not a person named Bao Ya.

proposals.before: In the fourth month of year 3 he was relieved as regent of Fuzhou.
proposals.after: In the fourth month of year 3 he was appointed regent of Fuzhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 除 means to appoint/install in office, not to relieve or remove from office.

proposals.before: Year 3, fourth month, removed as Fuzhou regent.
proposals.after: Year 3, fourth month, appointed Fuzhou regent.
proposals.reason: Chinese 除鄜州留後 means he was appointed Fuzhou regent; 除 is not 'removed.'

proposals.before: In the eleventh month he was given the Golden Pocket, Honored Equal to the Three Dukes, a thousand-household fief, and the Yanzhou command.
proposals.after: In the eleventh month he was given permission to open an office with honors equal to the Three Dukes, a thousand-household fief, and the Yanzhou command.
proposals.reason: Chinese 開府儀同三司 is Kaifu Yitong Sansi, not a 'Golden Pocket.'

proposals.before: Eleventh month, added Bearer of the Golden Pocket, Park-Walled Honored Equal to the Three Dukes, food domain one thousand households, appointed Yanzhou military commissioner.
proposals.after: Eleventh month, added Permitted to Open an Office with Honors Equal to the Three Dukes, food domain one thousand households, appointed Yanzhou military commissioner.
proposals.reason: Chinese 開府儀同三司 does not mean Bearer of the Golden Pocket or Park-Walled.

proposals.before: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: He was posthumously granted the title of Grand Preceptor.
proposals.reason: 冊贈 is posthumous bestowal of an honorific title, not feudal enfeoffment.

proposals.before: He was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: He was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor.
proposals.reason: 冊贈 denotes posthumous granting of a title, not enfeoffment.

proposals.before: His father Huan was Chamberlain for Dependencies and, through Tan's eminence, was repeatedly promoted to Left Vice Director.
proposals.after: His father Huan was Chamberlain for Dependencies and, through Tan's eminence, was repeatedly granted posthumous promotion to Left Vice Director.
proposals.reason: 累贈 is repeated posthumous bestowal, not promotion of a living official.

proposals.before: His father Huan was Chamberlain for Dependencies; because Tan was honored, he was repeatedly advanced to Left Vice Director.
proposals.after: His father Huan was Chamberlain for Dependencies; because Tan was honored, he was repeatedly granted posthumous advancement to Left Vice Director.
proposals.reason: 累贈 marks posthumous advancement, which the literal English omits.

proposals.before: In year 4 Yang Yanhong of Bian defeated Shang Rang and Li Kan outside Weishi Gate; Tan fought in the van, broke the enemy line, won the Founder's notice, and rose in rank.
proposals.after: In year 4 Yang Yanhong of Bian defeated Shang Rang and Li Dang outside Weishi Gate; Tan fought in the van, broke the enemy line, won the Founder's notice, and rose in rank.
proposals.reason: 李讜 is Li Dang; Kan is a wrong reading of 讜.

proposals.before: Year 4, Bian general Yang Yanhong defeated Chao generals Shang Rang and Li Kan outside the Weishi Gate; Tan was in the battle, shattered the van and broke the array, and thus came to the Founder's notice and gradually received promotion.
proposals.after: Year 4, Bian general Yang Yanhong defeated Chao generals Shang Rang and Li Dang outside the Weishi Gate; Tan was in the battle, shattered the van and broke the array, and thus came to the Founder's notice and gradually received promotion.
proposals.reason: 李讜 should be rendered Li Dang, not Li Kan.

proposals.before: In the seventh month he received the Golden Pocket, Honored Equal to the Three Dukes, honorary Grand Marshal, and princely rank of Langya; Zhao Yinheng brought the edict, with a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand taels of silver for holding Xing.
proposals.after: In the seventh month he was further granted Kaifu Yitong Sansi (Honored Equal to the Three Dukes), honorary Grand Marshal, and advancement to Prince of Langya; Zhao Yinheng brought the edict, with a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand taels of silver for holding Xing.
proposals.reason: 開府儀同三司 is Kaifu Yitong Sansi, not a Golden Pocket.

proposals.before: Seventh month, again added Bearer of the Golden Pocket, Park-Walled Honored Equal to the Three Dukes, honorary Grand Marshal, advanced to Prince of Langya commandery, ordered Palace Commissioner Zhao Yinheng to convey the edict in comfort, and bestowed one thousand bolts of silk and one thousand taels of silver—reward for defending Xingzhou.
proposals.after: Seventh month, again added Kaifu Yitong Sansi (Unbridled Office with Honors Equal to the Three Dukes), honorary Grand Marshal, advanced to Prince of Langya commandery, ordered Palace Commissioner Zhao Yinheng to convey the edict in comfort, and bestowed one thousand bolts of silk and one thousand taels of silver—reward for defending Xingzhou.
proposals.reason: 開府儀同三司 is mistranslated as Bearer of the Golden Pocket / Park-Walled.

proposals.before: In the sixth month the Prince of Jin took Weizhou and seized its dependencies; Hebei was in turmoil; Tan was ordered to advance with Liu Zhen of Kaifeng in support of Hebei.
proposals.after: In the sixth month the Prince of Jin took Weizhou and seized its dependencies; Hebei was in turmoil; Tan was ordered to advance with Liu Xun of Kaifeng in support of Hebei.
proposals.reason: Chinese 劉鄩 is Liu Xun (鄩 = Xún); the idiomatic English wrongly renders the given name as Zhen.

proposals.before: Sixth month, the Prince of Jin entered Weizhou and sent troops in divisions to take subordinate commanderies; Hebei was greatly disturbed; Tan received an edict with Kaifeng Intendant Liu Zhen to advance in pincer and aid Hebei.
proposals.after: Sixth month, the Prince of Jin entered Weizhou and sent troops in divisions to take subordinate commanderies; Hebei was greatly disturbed; Tan received an edict with Kaifeng Intendant Liu Xun to advance in pincer and aid Hebei.
proposals.reason: Chinese 劉鄩 is Liu Xun; the literal English wrongly renders 鄩 as Zhen.

proposals.before: Tan stormed Weixian in Chuan, captured it, and presented the rebel generals Li Yan and Wang Kaiguan.
proposals.after: Tan stormed Weixian in Chanzhou, captured it, and presented the rebel generals Li Yan and Wang Kaiguan.
proposals.reason: Chinese 澶州 is Chanzhou; idiomatic "Chuan" truncates the place-name and obscures the prefecture.

proposals.before: He was soon made deputy ambassador and acting commissioner of Tianping, with concurrent observation over Yan, Qi, and Cao.
proposals.after: He was soon made deputy ambassador and acting commissioner of Tianping, with concurrent observation over Yun, Qi, and Cao.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄆 is Yunzhou (Yun), not Yan; the idiomatic English misreads the prefecture name.

proposals.before: Soon he was appointed deputy ambassador of the Tianping army and acting military commissioner, concurrently Yan, Qi, and Cao circuit observation commissioner.
proposals.after: Soon he was appointed deputy ambassador of the Tianping army and acting military commissioner, concurrently Yun, Qi, and Cao circuit observation commissioner.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄆 is Yun, not Yan; the literal English misreads the prefecture name.

proposals.before: Soon he was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Preceptor, given the posthumous name Loyal Resolute, and buried on the Gaomen plateau in Kaifeng county.
proposals.after: Soon he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, given the posthumous name Loyal Resolute, and buried on the Gaomen plateau in Kaifeng county.
proposals.reason: Chinese 冊贈 is posthumous bestowal of office/honor, not feudal enfeoffment; "enfeoffed" misstates 贈.

decisions.reason: Focus unit has 潁州斤溝; 斤溝 is Jingou, not Jinchou. The proposed place-name romanization matches the Chinese and leaves the rest of the sentence intact.
Literal likewise misreads 斤溝 as Jinchou; Jingou is the correct reading of the native-place name in 潁州斤溝人也.
Chinese 鎮人 are men of Zhen, not the Jin, and 至深州而歸 returns from the prefecture Shenzhou, not 'deep in Zhao.' The proposed idiomatic restores both readings and the fuller wording of 先是…直抵鎮州城下…移軍掠….
Literal repeats the same errors: 鎮人 are Zhen men and 深州 is Shenzhou; the proposed replacement corrects both without inventing content.

Subject of 王言不克入 is the person Wang Yan (王言), already named in s0082–s0083; bare idiomatic 'Yan' wrongly looks like the place 鄆. The proposed wording matches the Chinese and the already-correct literal.
本名禮，太祖改而字之 states an original given name Li that the Founder changed and then styled; 'Born Li' is unnatural and omits the name change. The proposed sentence restores both 改 and 字之.
宣武軍 is the Xuanwu Army; Xuanyi misreads 武. The proposed 'Xuanwu commander' corrects the army name while preserving the rest.
Literal likewise has Xuanyi for 宣武軍; Xuanwu is the correct reading of the command title.
刺史保衙城 means the prefect held/defended the yamen citadel; 保衙 is not a personal name Bao Ya. The proposed idiomatic restores the verb phrase and the confusion of 不知所為.
Literal invents the same false personal name Bao Ya from 保衙城; 'held the yamen city' correctly parses 保 as the verb and 衙城 as the object.
除鄜州留後 in appointment formulae means he was installed as Fuzhou regent; 除 is not 'relieved.' The proposed 'appointed' matches the Chinese and the adjacent 授 / 遷 usages.
Literal 'removed as Fuzhou regent' reverses 除; the proposed 'appointed Fuzhou regent' is the correct office formula.

開府儀同三司 is the honor of being permitted to open an office with ceremonial parity to the Three Dukes; 'Golden Pocket' is a false gloss. The proposed phrasing restores that title without inventing other content.
Literal's 'Bearer of the Golden Pocket' and 'Park-Walled' invent sense absent from 開府儀同三司; the proposed English title matches the Chinese honor.
冊贈太師 is posthumous bestowal of the honorific title Grand Preceptor, not feudal enfeoffment; 'granted the title' correctly renders 冊贈.
Literal 'enfeoffed' likewise misstates 冊贈; 'posthumously granted Grand Preceptor' matches the Chinese.
累贈左僕射 is repeated posthumous advancement because of Tan's eminence; 'promoted' wrongly implies a living career step. The proposed wording restores 贈.
Literal omits that 累贈 is posthumous; adding 'posthumous advancement' corrects the meaning without other changes.
李讜 is conventionally Li Dang; Kan is a wrong reading of 讜. The proposed name fix is accurate and leaves the rest of the sentence intact.
Literal likewise has Li Kan for 李讜; Li Dang is the correct English form of the Chao general's name.
又加開府儀同三司 is further grant of Kaifu Yitong Sansi, not a 'Golden Pocket.' The proposed idiomatic restores that honor and keeps the remaining edict and reward content.

decisions.after: Seventh month, again added Kaifu Yitong Sansi (Permitted to Open an Office with Honors Equal to the Three Dukes), honorary Grand Marshal, advanced to Prince of Langya commandery, ordered Palace Commissioner Zhao Yinheng to convey the edict in comfort, and bestowed one thousand bolts of silk and one thousand taels of silver—reward for defending Xingzhou.
decisions.reason: Bearer of the Golden Pocket / Park-Walled wrongly invents 開府儀同三司, but the proposal's gloss 'Unbridled Office' is also inaccurate; revise to Kaifu Yitong Sansi with the same 'Permitted to Open an Office…' sense used for s0112.
劉鄩 is Liu Xun (鄩 = Xún); Zhen misreads the given name. The proposed idiomatic corrects only that name.
Literal likewise renders 鄩 as Zhen; Liu Xun is the correct reading of 劉鄩.
澶州 is Chanzhou; truncated idiomatic 'Chuan' obscures the prefecture. The proposed place-name matches 澶州魏縣.
鄆、齊、曹 names Yun, Qi, and Cao; idiomatic 'Yan' misreads 鄆. The proposed Yun restores the prefecture triad.
Literal likewise has Yan for 鄆; Yun is the correct reading in the observation-commissioner title.
冊贈太師 is posthumous grant of the title, not feudal enfeoffment; 'posthumously granted' correctly renders 冊贈 while leaving the posthumous name and burial intact.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0019 shows English Li Kan came only from misreading 讜; the personal-name claim must use Li Dang while keeping zh, pinyin, and claim identity fields.
The given-name claim must use Dang, the reading of 讜 restored by r0019.
Accepted r0023 shows English Liu Zhen came only from misreading 鄩; the personal-name claim must use Liu Xun while keeping zh, pinyin, and claim identity fields.
